paragraphs: The half litre bottle is the one people carry, and it is engineered for that: narrow enough for a hand or a cup holder, ribbed to stop the thin wall crumpling when gripped, and topped with a small cap that opens one handed. Those proportions are quite different from a bottle meant for a table.
The mesh is efficient at 17,953 polygons and 19,246 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the ribbing, the shoulder curve and the moulded base.
At $29 it suits beverage packaging visualisation, brand and label mockups, supermarket and e-commerce renders, sport and lifestyle imagery, and games. On sale since 2021.

A single disc floor machine is a motor over a rotating pad, with a long handle carrying the controls and a cable that never seems long enough. The head is heavy on purpose - the weight is what presses the pad into the floor - and the handle folds down so the machine can be wheeled.
The mesh is efficient at 24,675 polygons and 27,528 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the motor housing, the handle controls and the pad drive.

At $29 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits facility management and cleaning industry visualisation, commercial interior scenes, equipment marketing and catalogues, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2024.

Blank foil packets exist so that a designer can put artwork on them. The value is in the forms: a pillow pouch, a stand up pouch, a flat sachet, each with realistic crimped seals and the creases that foil takes when it is filled. Artwork applied to a flat rectangle never sits right.
The mesh is minimal at 6,592 polygons and 6,600 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry entirely in the seals and the fill creases.
At $29 it suits food and pharmaceutical packaging mockups, brand and label design presentation, retail and e-commerce renders, packaging industry marketing and games. On sale since 2023.

A plate of loose pulses is one of the most expensive things to model honestly, because there is no way to fake it: every bean has to be an object, sitting on the ones below at whatever angle it landed. That is why this asset carries 1,511,096 polygons and 1,418,776 vertices for what looks like a simple plate of food.

It is built in quads and tris with mixed UV layout and ships with 10 texture maps - 8 at 4096x4096 and 2 at 512x512 - carrying the split faces, the skins and the slight colour variation between individual beans.
At $29 it suits food photography and recipe visualisation, packaging and label mockups, nutrition and health material, grocery and wholesale renders, and games. On sale since 2020.

A single lens visor removes the bridge entirely, which is what makes it read as science fiction rather than as eyewear: a human face has two eyes and a nose between them, and a continuous band across both denies that. The metallic finish reinforces it by reflecting the environment rather than showing the eyes.
The mesh is minimal at 2,158 polygons and 2,224 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a smooth curved band whose whole effect comes from its material.

At $29 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits science fiction film and television, character design and games, fashion and editorial imagery, previsualisation and illustration. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a standard head. On sale since 2026.

A hose cart is a drum on a wheeled frame with a crank handle, a guide at the front and a short lead hose out of the hub that connects to the tap. That lead is the detail people forget: without it there is no way for water to reach a hose wound on a rotating drum.
The mesh is efficient at 24,572 polygons and 24,684 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 2 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the moulded plastic and the hose surface.
At $29 it suits garden and landscape visualisation, home exterior and utility scenes, garden equipment retail renders, lifestyle advertising and games. On sale since 2018.

A roller mixer keeps blood or culture samples gently agitated by rolling the tubes rather than shaking them, which is why the top is a bed of parallel rubber rollers rather than a platform. Tubes laid across them turn slowly and continuously, and that motion is the entire function of the machine.
The mesh is efficient at 32,418 polygons and 37,807 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the rollers, the drive housing and the control panel.

A rigged build sits on this page at the same $29 for when the rollers have to turn. Aimed at laboratory and clinical visualisation, medical device marketing, biotechnology presentation, science education material and games. On sale since 2021.

A gun safe is built around the length of what goes inside it, which makes it tall and narrow rather than cubic. The door is thick, the hinges are usually internal, there is a spoke handle and a keypad or dial, and the interior carries a barrel rest and a shelf above it.
The mesh runs 66,848 polygons and 68,082 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 8 texture maps carrying the powder coat finish, the handle and the keypad detail.
At $29 it suits home and firearms retail visualisation, security equipment marketing, interior and storage scenes, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2015.

A capless bulb has no metal base at all: the wires fold back against a moulded glass wedge that pushes straight into a socket. That construction makes it one of the smallest replaceable parts in a car, used in side lights, dashboards and number plate lamps, and it is instantly recognisable to anyone who has replaced one.

The mesh is minimal at 1,790 polygons and 1,804 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 6 texture maps at 4096x4096, which is a generous budget that goes entirely into the glass and the filament.
At $29 and built to StemCell specification, it suits automotive parts marketing and catalogues, workshop visualisation, technical illustration, retail renders and games. On sale since 2021.

A dermatoscope is a magnifier with its own light, designed to be pressed against skin so that surface reflection is eliminated and the structures underneath become visible. That is why the head has a contact plate, why the light ring surrounds the lens, and why the whole thing is shaped to be held like a pen rather than a torch.
The mesh is efficient at 21,385 polygons and 21,559 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the lens head, the contact plate and the grip knurling.
At $29 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits dermatology and clinical visualisation, medical device marketing, patient education material, clinic interiors and games. On sale since 2025.

The hip is a ball and socket, and its whole clinical interest is in that geometry: how deep the socket is, how the neck of the femur angles into it, and where the load passes. Isolating the joint from the rest of the skeleton is what lets that relationship be taught or explained without distraction.
The mesh is light at 5,312 polygons and 5,322 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a subject read through form rather than through surface detail.

Three rigged builds share this page at the same $29, including versions prepared for Cinema 4D and for Maya, which are the ones to take if the joint has to articulate. Aimed at orthopaedic and medical education, patient explanation, implant and device marketing, courseware and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2025.

A horizontal flow wrapper takes a product along a conveyor, folds a film around it, seals along the length and cuts between items. That sequence is laid out along the machine from infeed to discharge, which is why these machines are long and narrow and why the film reel sits above the middle.
The mesh runs 91,094 polygons and 95,769 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the film former, the sealing jaws and the conveyor.

At $29 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits food and packaging industry visualisation, machinery marketing and catalogues, production line scenes, technical and training material, and games. On sale since 2025.

A serving pitcher is a shape with two demanding features: a spout that pours cleanly without dribbling down the outside, and a handle that clears the body far enough for a full hand. Filled with iced tea it also becomes a refraction problem, since the liquid, the ice and the glass all bend light differently.
It is built with clean non-overlapping surfaces so the glass and the contents can each take their own material treatment rather than sharing one shell.
At $29 it suits beverage advertising, restaurant and hospitality visualisation, summer and lifestyle imagery, tableware retail renders, food photography set dressing and games. On sale since 2016.

A phone collection is more useful than a single handset because a product page, a comparison graphic or a retail display needs the range rather than one variant. Different sizes and finishes in one purchase also keep the proportions consistent between them, which matters when they appear side by side.
The models are supplied as a set so that colour variants and screen states can be swapped without rebuilding, which is exactly what a comparison layout needs.
At $29 it suits consumer electronics advertising, product and e-commerce renders, retail and comparison graphics, technology journalism, desk and interior scenes and games. On sale since 2019.
